nodes.summary: There are exactly four partitions with perimeter $3$, that is, four finite multisets of positive integers whose largest element plus number of elements (counted with multiplicity) equals $4$.
nodes.title: The partitions of perimeter three

nodes.summary: The perimeter of a partition is its largest part plus its number of parts minus $1$. For a natural number $n$, the partitions with perimeter $n$ form the finite set of all finite multisets $s$ of positive integers whose largest element plus number of elements (counted with multiplicity) equals $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Partitions with fixed perimeter

nodes.summary: Let $d$, $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 1$, $a \ge 1$, $2a < d + 3$ and $a \le n$. Then $\lfloor \lfloor (n - a)/(d + 1) \rfloor / 2 \rfloor \le \lfloor (n - a)/(d + 3) \rfloor$ and $\lfloor (\lfloor (n - a)/(d + 1) \rfloor + 1) / 2 \rfloor \le \lfloor (n + a)/(d + 3) \rfloor$.
nodes.title: A floor inequality for perimeter counts

nodes.summary: The partition $5 + 3$ has $2$-distinct parts, and the partition $4 + 3$ does not.
nodes.title: Examples of 2-distinct partitions

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number. A finite multiset $s$ of natural numbers has $d$-distinct parts when no element occurs in $s$ more than once and any two elements $x < y$ of $s$ satisfy $x + d \le y$.
nodes.title: Partitions into d-distinct parts

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $s$ a finite multiset of natural numbers. Then $s$ is a partition with perimeter $n$ if and only if every element of $s$ is positive and the largest element of $s$ (taken to be $0$ if $s$ is empty) plus the number of elements of $s$, counted with multiplicity, equals $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Membership in the partitions with fixed perimeter

nodes.summary: Take $d = a = 1$. Among the partitions with perimeter $3$, exactly two have $1$-distinct parts that are all at least $1$, exactly two have all parts congruent to $1$ modulo $2$, and exactly two have all parts congruent to $1$ or $-1$ modulo $4$. nodes.title: Small values of the fixed-perimeter partition counts

nodes.summary: Let $d$, $a$, $m$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 1$, $1 \le a \le d + 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$. Write $h_d^{(a)}(m, k)$ for the number of partitions into $d$-distinct parts, all at least $a$, with largest part $m$ and $k$ parts, and $f_d^{(a)}(m, k)$ for the number of partitions into parts congruent to $a$ modulo $d + 1$ with largest part $m$ and $k$ parts. nodes.title: Refined equality of distinct-part and residue counts

nodes.summary: Let $d$, $a$, $m$ and $k$ be positive integers with $a \le d + 1$, and write $h_d^{(a)}(m, k)$ for the number of partitions into $d$-distinct parts, all at least $a$, with largest part $m$ and $k$ parts. Then $h_d^{(a)}(m, k) \ne 0$ if and only if $m \ge a + d(k - 1)$, and in that case $h_d^{(a)}(m, k) = \binom{m - a - (d - 1)(k - 1)}{k - 1}$.
nodes.title: Counting d-distinct partitions by largest part and length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$, $m$ and $k$, $h_d^{(a)}(m, k)$ is the number of nonempty finite multisets of positive integers with largest element $m$, exactly $k$ elements counted with multiplicity, all elements at least $a$, and $d$-distinct parts. Such a partition has perimeter $m + k - 1$.
nodes.title: Partitions into d-distinct parts by largest part and length

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be positive integers and let $a$ be an integer with $1 \le a \le d + 1$. Then the number $h_d^{(a)}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ into $d$-distinct parts (no part repeats and any two parts differ by at least $d$), all at least $a$, equals the number $f_d^{(a)}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ into parts congruent to $a$ modulo $d + 1$. nodes.title: Fixed-perimeter identity for $d$-distinct parts

nodes.summary: Let $d$, $n$ and $a$ be positive integers with $a < (d + 3)/2$. Then the number $h_d^{(a)}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ into $d$-distinct parts (no part repeats and any two parts differ by at least $d$), all at least $a$, is at most the number $\ell_d^{(a)}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ into parts congruent to $a$ or $-a$ modulo $d + 3$. nodes.title: Reverse Alder-type inequality for fixed perimeter partitions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$ and $n$, let $h_d^{(a)}(n)$ be the number of partitions of perimeter $n$ (largest part plus number of parts minus $1$) into $d$-distinct parts, all at least $a$, where parts are $d$-distinct when no part repeats and any two parts differ by at least $d$. If $d$, $n$ and $a$ are positive, then $h_d^{(a+1)}(n) \le h_d^{(a)}(n)$, $h_{d+1}^{(a)}(n) \le h_d^{(a)}(n)$ and…
nodes.title: Monotonicity of fixed perimeter counts with $d$-distinct parts

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$ and $n$, $h_d^{(a)}(n)$ is the number of partitions of perimeter $n$ into $d$-distinct parts that are all at least $a$. Here the perimeter of a partition is its largest part plus its number of parts minus $1$, and a partition has $d$-distinct parts when no part repeats and any two parts differ by at least $d$.
nodes.title: Fixed perimeter partitions into $d$-distinct parts

nodes.summary: Let $d$, $a$, $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ be positive integers with $a < (d + 3)/2$, and let $\ell_d^{(a)}(\alpha, \lambda)$ be the number of partitions into parts congruent to $a$ or $-a$ modulo $d + 3$ with largest part $\alpha$ and exactly $\lambda$ parts. nodes.title: Nonvanishing and binomial count for parts $\equiv \pm a \pmod{d+3}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$, $\alpha$ and $\lambda$, $\ell_d^{(a)}(\alpha, \lambda)$ is the number of nonempty partitions into parts congruent to $a$ or $-a$ modulo $d + 3$ with largest part $\alpha$ and exactly $\lambda$ parts (so $\ell_d^{(a)}(0, 0) = 0$: the empty partition is not counted).
nodes.title: Partitions into parts $\equiv \pm a \pmod{d+3}$ by largest part and number of parts

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $d$ be an odd natural number and put $a = (d + 3)/2$. Then the number $\ell_d^{(a)}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ into parts congruent to $a$ or $-a$ modulo $d + 3$ is at most the number $h_d^{(a)}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ into $d$-distinct parts (no part repeats and any two parts differ by at least $d$), all at least $a$. nodes.title: Alder-type inequality in the degenerate case $a = (d + 3)/2$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$ and $n$, let $\ell_d^{(a)}(n)$ be the number of partitions of perimeter $n$ (largest part plus number of parts minus $1$) into parts congruent to $a$ or $-a$ modulo $d + 3$. If $d$, $n$ and $a$ are positive with $a < (d + 3)/2$, then $\ell_d^{(a)}(n) \le \ell_d^{(a)}(n + 1)$ and $\ell_{d+1}^{(a)}(n) \le \ell_d^{(a)}(n)$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of fixed perimeter counts with parts $\equiv \pm a \pmod{d+3}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$ and $n$, $\ell_d^{(a)}(n)$ is the number of partitions of perimeter $n$ into parts congruent to $a$ or $-a$ modulo $d + 3$, where the perimeter of a partition is its largest part plus its number of parts minus $1$.
nodes.title: Fixed perimeter partitions into parts $\equiv \pm a \pmod{d+3}$

nodes.title: Nonvanishing and binomial count for parts $\equiv a \pmod{d+1}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$, $m$ and $k$, $f_d^{(a)}(m, k)$ is the number of nonempty multisets of positive integers with largest part $m$ and exactly $k$ elements (counted with multiplicity), all of which are congruent to $a$ modulo $d + 1$.
nodes.title: Partitions into parts in one residue class, by largest part and length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $a$ and $n$, $f_d^{(a)}(n)$ is the number of partitions with perimeter $n$ all of whose parts are congruent to $a$ modulo $d + 1$. Here a partition is a nonempty multiset of positive integers, and its perimeter is its largest part plus its number of parts minus one.
nodes.title: Fixed perimeter partitions into parts in one residue class

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $k$, the map that sends a multiset $t$ of $k$ natural numbers to the multiset obtained from $t$ by adding one copy of $m$ is injective, so it embeds the multisets of size $k$ into all multisets of natural numbers.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
